markdown:
##### Source: Player's Handbook, [Dungeon Rollers' Improved Grappling](https://www.dmsguild.com/product/266037/Improved-Grappling), Neon City NightsThanks to Celica#1988 for the adjustments!

*Prerequisite: Strength 13 or higher*

You've developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits:

- When you move, you can drag or carry a grappled, but not restrained, creature with you at full movement speed, unless the creature is larger than you.
- While grappling a creature, if you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, you may replace any of your attacks with one of the special grapple actions listed below. Unless otherwise specified, special grapple actions require a free hand to initiate them, in addition to having a creature already grappled.
  - **Restrain.** You can attempt to restrain a creature grappled by you. Make a grapple check. If you succeed, the creature is restrained, and you move at half movement speed until the grapple ends or you willingly end the restrained condition on them. A creature restrained in this way cannot use their hands as a somatic component for spells.
  - **Gag.** Covering the creature’s mouth, you try to stop it from verbalizing, either by jamming your forearm into their mouth, squeezing their neck, squeezing their face, or any other method of gagging. Make a grapple check. If you succeed, the creature suffers the silenced effect until the end of your next turn. If the creature breaks free from your grapple, the silence effect immediately ends.
  - **Pound.** You can take a swing at a creature you have grappled. Make a melee attack against the creature you have grappled. You may always make an unarmed strike in this way, even if you do not have any free hands available. If the attack is made using a light weapon or unarmed strike, you have advantage on the attack.
  - **Throw Prone.** You can attempt to throw a creature grappled by you to the ground. Make a grapple check. If you succeed, the creature is no longer grappled, but is knocked prone in a square of your choosing within 10 feet of you.
  - **Disarm.** You can attempt to rid your opponent of a troublesome item. Target an item held by the grappled creature and make a grapple check. If you succeed, the defender drops the item on the ground. If you succeed in the contest by more than 5, you may instead choose to take the item. You have disadvantage if the defender is holding the item with two or more hands. The target has advantage if it is larger than you, or disadvantage if it is smaller.
  - **Subdue.** While you are grappling someone who is restrained, an ally can attempt to subdue the target using ropes or manacles. The friendly creature uses their action to make a contested grapple check. If the ally succeeds, they can inflict the incapacitated effect on the target and immediately apply the manacles or rope to bind them. While incapacitated in this way, a creature may attempt to break the equipment subduing them and take any other actions as normal while they are subdued with manacles or rope. This effect lasts until either the subdued creature is freed, or they escape the equipment used.
